sentences.text: Perused the record.

This repeat application for bail has been filed by applicant Ramu seeking his enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 256 of 2015, under Sections 363, 366, 376, 342 IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act,
Police Station- Anwala, District Bareilly during the pendency of trial.
At the very outset, the learned A.G.A. contends that notice of present application for bail has been served upon first informant/opposite party-2.
However, inspite of service of notice no one has put in appearance on behalf o ffirst informant/opposite party-2 to oppose this application for bail.

sentences.text:
For ready reference same is reproduced herein under:
"This is an application for bail moved on behalf of the accused-applicant, Ramu involved in Case Crime No. 256 of 2015, under sections 363, 366, 376, 342 IPC and 5/6 POCSO Act, P.S. Anwala, District Bareilly.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate and perused the record.

Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that in the present case co-accused,
Dinesh is the main culprit while the present applicant helps the prosecutrix.
I have gone through the statement of prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.,
in her deposition, she has specifically levelled the allegation of committing rape against the present applicant and other co-accused.
Learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail.
Having considered the facts and circumstances of the case, without recording any finding on merit, I do not find any good ground to release the applicant on bail.
The application for bail is hereby rejected. "
The second bail application of applicant was rejected vide order dated 17.2.2020, passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 5341 of 2018 (Ramu Vs State of U.P.).

sentences.text:
For ready reference, same is reproduced herein under:
"Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on the record.
Applicant-

Ramu seeks bail in Case Crime No. 256 of 2015, under Sections 363, 366,
376, 342 I.P.C. and Section 5/6 POCSO Act, Police Station- Anwala, District- Bareilly.
This is the second bail application on behalf of the applicant.
The first bail was rejected by the Court vide order dated 13.11.2017.
Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the prayer for the bail.
In the facts and circumstances of the case, I do not find any fresh ground to consider the prayer for bail of the applicant.
The prayer for bail is declined.

Ramu vs State Of U.P. on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60604191/
2
The second application for bail is, hereby, rejected without expressing any opinion on the merit of the case.

However, considering the fact that applicant is languishing in jail since 13.1.2017, the trial court is directed to expedite the trial of aforesaid case and conclude the same in accordance with law without granting unnecessary adjournments to either of the parties as expeditiously as possible preferably within a period of six months from the date of production of a certified copy of this order, if there is no legal impediment. "

Learned counsel for applicant submits that inspite of the specific direction issued by this Court vide order dated 17.2.2020, to conclude the trial within a period of six months from the date of production of certified copy of this order, the trial has not yet concluded.
Applicant is in jail since 13.11.2017.
As such, he has undergone six years and eight months of incarceration.

Referring to the judgement of Supreme court in A.R. Antulay Vs. R.S. Nayak (1992) 1 SCC 225, he submits that since an accused has the right to speedy trial and the said right of the accused/applicant stands infringed on account of lackadaisical approach of the prosecution, he therefore contends that applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.

entities.text: A.R. Antulay Vs. R.S. Nayak (1992) 1 SCC 225
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In case the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misused the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.
Even otherwise, applicant is a man of clean antecedents inasmuch as he has no criminal history to his credit except the present one.
Applicant is in jail since 13.1.2017.
As such, he has undergone more than six years and eight months of incarceration.

Police report in terms of Section 173 (2)
Cr.P.C. has already been submitted against applicant, as such, the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by prosecution against applicant stands crystalized.
However, up to this stage, no such circumstance has emerged necessitating the custodial arrest of applicant during the pendency of trial.
It is thus urged that in case applicant is enlarged on bail he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with trial.
Per contra, the learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail.
He submits that from the perusal of order dated 13.11.2017, passed by this Court, it is apparent that applicant is main accused.
The prosecutrix is a young girl aged about 14 years, 4 months and 16 days on the date of occurrence.
Attention of the Court was then invited to the order sheet of concerned Sessions Court, copy of which is on record as Annexure-10 to the affidavit filed in support of present application.
On the basis of above, it is sought to be contended that the Trial could not be concluded only because of non appearance of applicant on the dates fixed.
As such, prosecution cannot be held responsible for the delay in trial.
The ratio laid down in above mentioned case is thus not attracted.
No new or good ground is made to enlarge the applicant on bail.
As such, the bail application is liable to be rejected.
When confronted with above, the learned counsel for applicant could not overcome the same.

Having heard the learned counsel for applicants, the learned A.G.A. for State, upon perusal of material brought on record, evidence, nature and gravity of offence as well as complicity of applicant, accusation made coupled with the fact that since applicant himself has failed to appear before Court below on the date fixed which fact is clearly explicit from the order sheet, there being Ramu vs State Of U.P. on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60604191/
3 nothing on record to contradict the orders contained in the order sheet, prima facie the ratio laid down by Supreme court in the case of A.R. Antulay (Supra) is not attracted.
As such, no new or good ground is made out to enlarge the applicant on bail.

As a result, the bail application fails and is liable to rejected It is accordingly rejected.
Order Date :- 15.9.2023
